papers.abstract: Long-context models use sparse or structured attention to avoid quadratic cost, yet retrieving a small set of relevant facts embedded among hundreds of thousands of distractors degrades as normalization mass disperses with length. Hub-and-spoke optimal transport (OT) replaces the dense $L \times L$ matrix with a linear-size graph over local windows and $K$ shared hubs balanced by Sinkhorn scaling. Building on block-wise tail refinement and fixed-support transport topology (arXiv:2605.08123, arXiv:2609.07954), we introduce Topology Hub Optimal Transport (THOT): (1) bounded-support capacity gating via simplex sparsemax ($O(L\log L)$) or sorting-free token-local thresholded ReLU ($O(L)$), driving excess distractor mass to zero; (2) a three-sweep $1+2$ annealed row-closed Sinkhorn schedule that damps bipartite residuals; (3) an exact rank-$(D+2R+1)$ One-Reference-Tile adjoint in batched split-factor Triton kernels (BF16 Tensor Cores, FP32 potentials); and (4) a chunked exclusive-prefix causal variant with verified zero future leakage. On NVIDIA L4, sparsemax THOT trained at $L=128$ reaches 97.40% zero-shot recall of fixed bindings at $L=262{,}144$ under pure task loss ($\alpha=0$) and 98.83% at $\alpha=0.05$ (matched by $O(L)$ thresholded ReLU at $\alpha=0.05$, vs. 80.60% at $\alpha=0$), while softmax-gated hub OT drops to 3.52%. In bidirectional operator microbenchmarks, our kernel runs forward+VJP in 100.1 ms at $H=8, D=64, L=262\mathrm{K}$ (2.2x faster with 4.0x smaller compiler temporaries than latent softmax) and 1.34 ms vs. 4.37 ms for cuDNN FlashAttention at $L=4{,}096$; multi-layer LM runs use the unfused path. Zero-shot WikiText-103 multi-needle retrieval hits 100.00% (128/128 queries at $L=65\mathrm{K}$) vs. 0.78% for short-trained RoPE FlashAttention, and compact 4-layer WikiText-4K runs show modest causal and masked LM gains.
bullets: Addresses long-context retrieval degradation caused by attention normalization mass spreading across distractors.
Builds a linear-size local-window-plus-hub transport graph with sparsemax or thresholded-ReLU gating to eliminate excess distractor mass.
Adds annealed Sinkhorn updates, an exact low-rank adjoint, fused Triton kernels, and a causal chunked variant with zero future leakage.
At 262K tokens, sparsemax THOT achieves 97.40% or 98.83% fixed-binding recall depending on loss regularization, while softmax-gated hub OT reaches 3.52%.
Reports 100% multi-needle retrieval on 65K-token WikiText-103 queries and faster operator benchmarks than the compared baselines; broader multi-layer LM runs use an unfused path.

papers.selection_reason: Introduces hub optimal transport with sparse gating for long-context attention, directly targeting long-context models and efficient attention.
papers.title: Topology Hub Optimal Transport: Eliminating Long Context Dilution at Flash Speed
papers.tldr: THOT uses sparse capacity-gated hub optimal transport and optimized kernels to preserve relevant facts in extremely long contexts while reducing attention overhead.

papers.abstract: Anchor tokens let a vision transformer exchange global information through a few summaries, but nothing forces different anchors to summarise different things. On one shared backbone we show that a Perceiver-style pathway and an AnchorFormer pathway collapse to a single summary, the latter despite its mass normalisation (pooling-map similarity 0.99), while other soft pathways, including Representative Attention, stay partly redundant (0.59-0.79). These results concern the routing modules inside our block, not the full published models. An exclusive partition of the patch grid cannot collapse by construction, and matched component by component it is 2.4-3.6 points more accurate than Representative Attention on CIFAR-100. We then propose focus anchors, which place most anchors at the peaks of a learned importance map while all anchors keep one exclusive Voronoi partition. Focus anchors beat a fixed partition on a cluttered canvas (+1.5 points, 95% CI [0.5, 2.6]) but not on full-HD traffic-sign recognition. There, both variants match dense attention with local windows at about a fifth of its FLOPs, and the fixed partition also trains 1.5x faster per step than dense attention with FlashAttention, though both use more memory; a ViT on a downsampled input loses half its mean average precision. Hard exclusive assignment is the only region assignment we tested that is both stable and most accurate: softmax and Sinkhorn relaxations diverge, and Gumbel-softmax trains but is less accurate. We also report the limits: a ResNet-18 is more accurate on every task we trained it on in this from-scratch regime, and anchors train faster than FlashAttention only from about 1536x1536 pixels and never use less memory.
bullets: Soft anchor-routing pathways can produce highly redundant summaries, whereas exclusive patch partitions prevent collapse by construction.
The proposed focus anchors concentrate anchors near learned importance peaks while preserving exclusive Voronoi regions.
On CIFAR-100, exclusive routing is 2.4–3.6 points more accurate than Representative Attention; focus anchors add 1.5 points on a cluttered canvas.
For full-HD traffic-sign recognition, both anchor variants match dense local-window attention at about one-fifth the FLOPs; fixed partitions train 1.5× faster per step.
Hard exclusive assignment was the most stable and accurate tested option, but anchors use more memory and do not outperform the trained ResNet-18 in this regime.

papers.selection_reason: Anchor-based routing with exclusive region assignment reduces attention cost in vision transformers, an efficient-attention contribution.
papers.title: Anchors That Move Without Collapsing: Exclusive-Region Anchor Routing for Vision Transformers
papers.tldr: Exclusive region assignment prevents anchor collapse in vision transformers, while focus-based placement can improve performance on cluttered scenes but is not universally beneficial.

papers.abstract: Retrieval-based sparse attention, exemplified by DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA), reduces attention computation by selecting a small subset of key-value entries. However, selecting these entries can still require searching the entire visible history. For long sequences, retrieval becomes a major bottleneck, limiting the efficiency gains from sparse attention. To address this problem, we propose LongCat Recall Sparse Attention (LRSA), which combines fine-grained representatives with paged retrieval in an incrementally maintained index. LRSA partitions the sequence into time buckets that can be indexed independently as new keys arrive, without regrouping existing history. Within each bucket, it organizes indexing keys into capacity-balanced directional groups and packs a fixed number of complete groups into each page, retaining a separate center for every group. These centers provide fine-grained representatives for page selection, after which refinement scores members of the selected pages together with sink, sliding-window, and visible unindexed candidates to select the final Top-$K$ logical positions. To execute this retrieval process efficiently, we store members in reordered pages, fuse construction stages according to group size, and share storage for overlapping fixed candidates across queries during chunked prefill. These choices support regular member access while reducing kernel launches during construction and repeated candidate transfers. Moreover, we integrate LRSA into SGLang to maintain the index during inference, overlapping asynchronous index construction for new buckets with subsequent computation and reusing compatible bucket indices and member pages after a prefix match in the original key-value pool. With a 1024K-token context, LRSA accelerates key selection by 4.70$\times$ over DSA and combined selection and attention by 35.60$\times$ over full attention.
authors: Hao Zhang, Bin Xiao, Kefeng Zhang
bullets: Problem: Sparse attention can reduce computation, but searching the entire visible history makes key retrieval a bottleneck for very long contexts.

Method: Partition history into independently indexed time buckets, organize keys into balanced directional groups, and use group centers for coarse page selection before refining candidates to select Top-K positions.
Implementation: Reordered pages, fused index-construction stages, shared fixed-candidate storage, and asynchronous index maintenance improve retrieval and inference efficiency.
Result: At 1024K-token context, LRSA accelerates key selection 4.70× over DSA and combined selection plus attention 35.60× over full attention.
Scope: The reported gains target long-context inference with incrementally arriving keys and prefix reuse.

papers.selection_reason: Introduces LongCat Recall Sparse Attention (LRSA) to improve retrieval efficiency for long-context LLM inference.
papers.title: LongCat Recall Sparse Attention: Co-Designing Key Organization and Retrieval for Long-Context Inference
papers.tldr: LRSA makes long-context sparse attention substantially faster by co-designing an incrementally maintained, paged retrieval index with efficient GPU execution.

papers.abstract: The Query-derived Erase Direction (QED) augments a rank-one linear attention update with a key-orthogonal query component. Under scalar decay, this correction leaves the eigenvalues of each homogeneous state transition unchanged, while the propagation of an initial perturbation depends on the ordered product of these transitions. We construct a periodic token sequence with fixed key and query projections for which every one-step spectral radius is below one but the spectral radius of the period product exceeds one. The same construction yields a sufficient condition for mean-square growth under independent uniform token sampling. For rank-one erasure with channel-wise decay, we derive a necessary and sufficient spectral-norm test for one-step nonexpansiveness that can be evaluated in $O(d)$ time. The test agrees with direct singular value decomposition on all 1,800 operators evaluated. In a counterfactual replay of a selected head of Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base, the terminal gain on a 4,096-token repeated-text sequence increased from 0.99938 to 1.3977 with the feature and checkpoint gate trajectories held fixed.
bullets: Shows a periodic sequence where every transition has spectral radius below one, yet the period product is expansive.
Extends the construction to sufficient conditions for mean-square growth under independent uniform token sampling.
Derives a necessary-and-sufficient spectral-norm criterion for channel-wise-decay rank-one erasure, computable in O(d) time.
The criterion matched direct SVD on all 1,800 tested operators.
In a Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base replay, terminal gain rose from 0.99938 to 1.3977 under repeated text with feature and gate trajectories fixed.

papers.title: Recurrent Amplification and Exact Nonexpansiveness Criteria for Query-Driven Erasure

papers.abstract: Recent gated linear attention models use state-independent gates, computed from token representations without directly reading the recurrent memory. This design supports efficient chunkwise computation: sequences are divided into chunks of consecutive tokens, with parallel computation within each chunk. However, the same token representation produces the same gate, even when the layer stores different information. We introduce State-Dependent Gating (SDG), which computes element-wise gates from the change in memory over a chunk and applies them at the chunk boundary. This provides state feedback for forgetting while preserving parallel computation within each chunk. We develop fused kernels for Gated DeltaNet, Kimi Delta Attention, Gated DeltaNet-2, and Mamba-3. Our theoretical analysis quantifies the potential reconstruction benefits of state-dependent, element-wise gating under a signal--noise model. We also show that boundary decay is an element-wise ridge proximal step when the gate is held fixed. Empirical evaluation of 1.3B linear attention and hybrid models trained on 100B tokens shows improvements across language modeling, commonsense reasoning, synthetic and real-world retrieval, and long-context understanding. These results demonstrate that SDG is an effective approach to enhancing existing linear attention models.
authors: Renjia Deng, Yuxi Liu, Yutong He, Xue Wang, Kun Yuan
bullets: Existing gated linear attention uses state-independent gates, which ignore the information currently stored in recurrent memory.
SDG computes element-wise gates from the memory change over each chunk and applies them at the chunk boundary.
The approach preserves parallel within-chunk computation and is implemented with fused kernels for several linear-attention architectures.
Theory connects SDG to improved signal reconstruction and interprets fixed-gate boundary decay as an element-wise ridge proximal step.
Experiments on 1.3B models trained on 100B tokens report improvements across language modeling, reasoning, retrieval, and long-context understanding.

papers.selection_reason: State-dependent gating improves linear attention efficiency and long-context modeling, directly relevant to efficient attention and LLM architectures.
papers.title: SDG: State-Dependent Gating at Chunk Boundaries for Linear Attention
papers.tldr: State-Dependent Gating improves chunkwise linear attention by using memory changes to control element-wise forgetting without sacrificing parallel computation within chunks.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward models have been very successful in 3D reconstruction with ad hoc attention designs that relate all view patches densely. However, the cost of this dense global attention grows quadratically with the number of views, preventing the model from applying to larger-scale reconstruction settings. In this paper, we argue that most dense attention computations are unnecessary from a classical structure-from-motion perspective: 3D structures stem from geometrically matching regions in 2D. We bring this principle to learning-based feed-forward reconstruction with our Sparse Geometric Attention Reconstruction (SGAR) method. In SGAR, each patch token attends to only a small set of patch tokens from other views, chosen by a lightweight learned key selection module trained to predict cross-view 3D proximity of tokens. Thus, dense global attention is replaced by much more efficient geometric-similarity-guided sparse attention. SGAR is a general method that can be applied to different feed-forward models by fine-tuning. In our experiments, we show that SGAR is the fastest among both state-of-the-art dense and sparse methods and the most accurate sparse one. It runs up to 12-times faster than dense attention at 1,000 views with stable pose accuracy where existing sparse methods fail, and shows the best performance in reconstructing more complete geometries on the same time budget.
authors: Aoxiang Fan, Maria Pilligua, Corentin Dumery, Oliver Heinimann, Pascal Fua
bullets: Dense global attention scales quadratically with the number of views, limiting large-scale reconstruction.
A lightweight key-selection module predicts cross-view 3D proximity and selects only relevant patch tokens.
The approach can be integrated into different feed-forward reconstruction models through fine-tuning.
Experiments report the fastest runtime among compared dense and sparse methods, with the strongest accuracy among sparse methods.
At 1,000 views, SGAR runs up to 12× faster than dense attention while maintaining stable pose accuracy and producing more complete geometry under equal time budgets.

figures.caption: Figure 4. Qualitative comparison. Point clouds predicted by FastVGGT, ZipMap and SGAR (DejaView), with the ground truth, on one scene of each of 7-Scenes (chess/seq-03), ETH3D (courtyard, laser scan), LaMAR (HGE) and Mip-NeRF 360 (bonsai, SfM points). Left: four of the input views. Below each reconstruction: the AUC@30 of its cameras. SGAR (DejaView) keeps the structure of the scene where the other efficient models fragment it, most visibly on the long LaMAR trajectory.

Figure 3. Overview of SGAR. We replace the global dense attention of DejaView [8] with our sparse geometric attention as an example. The images are encoded by DINOv2 and augmented with camera and register tokens. A single shared block, unrolled over its L steps, runs frame attention, key selection and sparse attention. In sparse attention, each patch attends to the special tokens of all views, the patches of the reference view, a summary of each cluster, and all the patches of the nearest clusters, so that its cost grows near-linearly with the number of views. Key Selection projects the patch tokens by Wadj into a geometric embedding and clusters the embeddings by spherical k-means into √ N clusters, re-clustered at every step. Each cluster probes its m = 4 nearest clusters, itself first. With the patches sorted by cluster, the selected keys form a block-sparse mask over tiles of 128 tokens. A contrastive loss pulls together the embeddings of patches that observe the same surface in the ground-truth geometry and pushes the others apart.

papers.abstract: Attention in large language models (LLMs) scores every query against every key with a full dot product. We investigate whether this dot product must be computed completely for attention to be effective. We propose Hidden Sparse Attention (HiSA), which keeps the query and key projections intact but only computes a partial dot product, following a static, parameter-free rule set by the token positions: attention becomes sparse in the hidden (feature) dimension, an axis much less explored than token sparsity, rather than over tokens as in almost all sparse attention methods. Based on the structure of rotary position embeddings (RoPE), we decompose keys and queries into parts which can be omitted when computing attention. By training LLMs from scratch with HiSA, we find that this partial dot product does not hurt but improves performance compared with the complete product while computing only about a third of the query-key products. During inference HiSA improves decoding speed and shrinks memory footprint. We also extend HiSA to FlashAttention-3 kernels for training and inference. Finally, we motivate our approach by showing that dense attention learns to suppress the attention score parts that HiSA drops. Code is available at https://github.com/ambroise-b/hisa.
authors: Ambroise Borbely, Mathieu Salzmann, Olivier Verscheure
bullets: Targets the full query-key dot product in LLM attention rather than sparsifying across tokens.
Uses a static, parameter-free rule based on token positions and RoPE structure to omit selected query/key components.
Preserves full query and key projections while computing only a partial attention score.
Training from scratch shows no performance loss and reported improvements over complete dot products.
Extends to FlashAttention-3 and reduces decoding time and memory usage; dense attention also learns to suppress the omitted components.

papers.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) increasingly need to process long documents and codebases, making long-context attention a major prefill bottleneck. Block sparse attention reduces computation by skipping unimportant blocks of the attention matrix, but scoring blocks accurately can itself be expensive. We propose Delta-Based Tile Scoring (DTS), a training-free, content-adaptive tile scoring method for sparse block attention. DTS selects query and key anchors according to local vector changes, using fewer representatives in redundant regions while retaining more detail in heterogeneous regions. To accelerate anchor selection, parallel delta packing partitions the query and key sequences into tile-aligned chunks and performs bounded local scans over these chunks concurrently. The selected tiles are then computed using the original query, key, and value vectors. On LLaMA-3.1-8B-Instruct, DTS keeps average RULER and LongBench scores within 0.10 percentage points of full attention, with RULER evaluated up to 128K tokens. At 128K tokens, DTS reduces measured scoring-pipeline latency by 38% compared with XAttention. On four NVIDIA H100 GPUs, it achieves a 3.3$\times$ prefill speedup over a PyTorch full-attention baseline using FlashAttention-2 at 512K tokens.
authors: Emre U\u{g}ur, Jiawen Qi, Qinyu Chen
bullets: Addresses the prefill bottleneck of long-context attention, where accurately scoring skippable blocks can be costly.
Uses training-free, content-adaptive delta scoring with fewer anchors in redundant regions and more in heterogeneous ones.
Accelerates scoring through parallel, tile-aligned local scans, then computes selected tiles with the original vectors.
Maintains average RULER and LongBench scores within 0.10 percentage points of full attention, including RULER up to 128K tokens.
Reports 38% lower scoring-pipeline latency than XAttention at 128K tokens and 3.3× prefill speedup over a FlashAttention-2 PyTorch baseline at 512K tokens on four H100 GPUs.

papers.abstract: We study the problem of computational efficiency for linear bandits in high-dimensional settings with a finite arm set. In linear bandits, the increase in the dimension $d$ of the feature vectors leads to growing computational costs of $O(d^2)$ at each round of update. Traditional low-rank approximation methods such as SOFUL reduce computation via fixed-size matrix sketching, yet run the risk of incurring vacuous linear regret when the spectral tail of the data is heavy and the approximation rank is inadequately selected. To guarantee regret convergence and effectively reduce computational costs, we introduce a clustering mechanism and propose the Coordinate Basis Linear Bandit (CBL) algorithm. Our method preserves the full covariance information in each cluster by maintaining an exact orthonormal basis of the cluster's column space together with a low-dimensional coordinate representation, which guarantees robust sublinear regret without spectral-tail vulnerabilities. It performs cluster switching by assigning a sentinel for each cluster, and reduces per-round update computation to $O(\bar r^2)$ in the cluster's effective dimension $\bar r=\min(r,l)$, where $r$ is the intrinsic rank of the data and $l<d$ is a tunable rank bound.
authors: Hantao Yang, Hong Xie, Defu Lian
bullets: Targets the $O(d^2)$ per-round update cost of high-dimensional linear bandits.
Avoids the vacuous linear regret risk of fixed-rank sketching under heavy spectral tails.
Maintains an exact orthonormal basis and low-dimensional coordinates for each cluster.
Uses cluster sentinels for switching and reduces updates to $O(\bar r^2)$, where $\bar r=\min(r,l)$.
The abstract states sublinear regret and computational savings, but gives no numerical experimental results.
papers.selection_reason: Proposes a clustering mechanism (Coordinate Basis Linear Bandit) to reduce computational costs in high-dimensional linear bandits, improving efficiency.
papers.title: Coordinate Basis Linear Bandits with Sublinear Regret over Low-Rank Clusters
papers.tldr: CBL accelerates finite-arm linear bandits by clustering arms and preserving exact low-dimensional covariance structure, achieving robust sublinear regret without spectral-tail failures.

papers.abstract: Hybrid attention models combine full and linear attention to achieve a better quality--efficiency trade-off. Converting pretrained Transformers into such models requires identifying which layers should retain full attention under a prescribed budget. We identify two off-policy mismatches in FlashMorph's layer selection: (i) continuous branch interpolation and teacher-forced hidden states differ from discrete hybrid computation; and (ii) frozen model weights fail to account for parameter adaptation during subsequent recovery. We introduce FlashMorph2, an on-policy layer-selection method that (I) evaluates sampled discrete hybrid architectures end to end using their own hidden states, and (II) jointly optimizes layer-selection scores and model weights under the recovery objective to reflect post-adaptation performance. Experiments across Qwen3 model scales and linear-attention variants show that FlashMorph2 consistently outperforms existing layer-selection methods, improving average scores over FlashMorph by $+2.42$ points on RULER, $+1.08$ on LongBench, and $+0.76$ on recall-intensive tasks, while completing layer selection in only $0.72$--$3.57$ GPU hours across 0.6B--8B models, demonstrating high efficiency and scalability.
authors: Disen Lan, Xuanda Wang, Jianbin Zheng, Huafeng Kuang, Wei Tang, Yu Cheng
bullets: Hybrid attention models need to choose which layers retain full attention under a compute budget.
FlashMorph2 evaluates discrete hybrid architectures end to end using their own hidden states, avoiding off-policy selection errors.
It jointly optimizes layer-selection scores and model weights to reflect performance after recovery.
Across Qwen3 scales and linear-attention variants, it improves over FlashMorph by 2.42 RULER points, 1.08 LongBench points, and 0.76 points on recall-intensive tasks.
Layer selection takes 0.72–3.57 GPU hours for 0.6B–8B models, indicating efficient scaling.

papers.abstract: Long video sequences make attention a substantial cost in video diffusion models. Block sparse attention (BSA) reduces this cost by computing selected blocks exactly while compressing the remaining blocks. However, fixed token grouping can place tokens with dissimilar attention preferences in the same group, while uniform key averaging can underestimate the attention mass of compressed blocks. We introduce Spark-Attn, a training-free BSA method comprising Spark-Reblock and Spark-Reweight. Spark-Reblock recursively groups tokens by attention preference while preserving regular block shapes for efficient GPU execution. Spark-Reweight uses the global mean query as an anchor to construct attention-weighted key-value representations and logit biases for the compressed blocks, calibrating their attention mass. We instantiate Spark-Attn in MiniMax-H3 as Spark-H3. At 10% exact-block density, Spark-H3 delivers a 2.49$\times$ DiT speedup and reaches 24.81 dB PSNR against the corresponding dense outputs on MiniMax-H3 (20 denoising steps, 345 frames, 1344$\times$768). Increasing the density to 20% further improves PSNR to 26.76 dB while still achieving a 2.26$\times$ DiT speedup. These results demonstrate that Spark-H3 achieves a state-of-the-art quality-efficiency trade-off for training-free BSA on video diffusion models.
authors: Zecheng Tang, Jiaye Fu, Youtian Lin, Xinyao Rao, Liuxuan Sun, Jian Zhang, Yao Yao, Wei Li
bullets: Targets the high attention cost of long video sequences in diffusion models.
Spark-Reblock recursively groups tokens with similar attention preferences while retaining GPU-friendly regular blocks.
Spark-Reweight uses a global-mean-query anchor to build weighted key-value summaries and calibrate compressed-block attention mass.
At 10% exact-block density, it achieves a 2.49× DiT speedup and 24.81 dB PSNR versus dense outputs.
At 20% density, PSNR rises to 26.76 dB with a 2.26× speedup; the method is training-free and instantiated in MiniMax-H3.

papers.abstract: VGGT reconstructs cameras and geometry from unposed images in one pass, but its global attention grows quadratically with the number of views. Training-free accelerators thin this attention and work well on redundant video, but lose pose accuracy when views share little geometry. This paper traces these losses to two kinds of cross-view information that a uniform sparse approximation can fail to preserve together: diffuse layers aggregate distributed context, whereas matching layers depend on query-specific interactions that carry little attention mass. A per-layer statistic measures the log-mass missed by a mean token. Its row-free proxy is the logit variance, and it selects the estimator for each layer. Diffuse layers use shared, importance-sampled hub keys, with log-weights that make the softmax numerator and denominator unbiased. Matching layers stay exact: every aggressive thinning tested cost accuracy. At equal cost, the selected layers outperform the four shifted windows tested. On 13 unseen low-redundancy scenes with 32 views, LMSA stays within 1.4 AUC@5 of dense attention, compared with 10.3 for AVGGT and 4.5 for SAF3R; its difference from contemporaneous GPA-VGGT is not significant, and only its gains over AVGGT pass both scene-level tests. With 100 views, it stays within 1.9 AUC@5 while its aggregator runs $2.0\times$ faster. Used post hoc to choose the layers GPA-VGGT protects, the statistic improves it by 1.2 AUC@5 for 5% more FLOPs. Applied untuned to $\pi^3$, it beats AVGGT but remains further from dense accuracy.
authors: Sammam Mahdi, Fariha Binta Salim, K. M. Jubair Sami, Rakin Bin Rabbani
bullets: Uniform attention thinning can lose pose accuracy when views share little geometry.
A logit-variance statistic selects between shared importance-sampled hubs for diffuse layers and exact attention for matching layers.
On 13 unseen 32-view scenes, LMSA stayed within 1.4 AUC@5 of dense attention, versus 10.3 for AVGGT and 4.5 for SAF3R.
With 100 views, it remained within 1.9 AUC@5 of dense attention while running 2.0× faster in aggregation.
The statistic also improved GPA-VGGT by 1.2 AUC@5 at 5% more FLOPs, but untuned transfer to π³ remained farther from dense accuracy.

papers.abstract: Compact convolutional backbones such as EfficientNet achieve strong parameter efficiency through local depthwise separable convolutions, yet two structural questions remain central to hybrid design: where does global self-attention improve recognition over pure convolution, and can repeated blocks share weights without losing representational capacity? We investigate both questions on ImageNet-1k (50,000-image validation) using controlled EfficientNet-B0 experiments. First, we show that wrapping a classification backbone in multi-scale feature pyramids (BiFPN) fails to outperform a plain MBConv trunk (69.99% - 71.81% vs. 72.86% plain B0) until paired with stage attention (73.15%). In contrast, keeping the MBConv trunk intact and inserting lightweight zero-gated residual self-attention adapters at stages P3 (28x28 windowed), P4 (14x14 global), and P5 (7x7 global) reaches 74.02% standalone and outperforms a bit-for-bit matched plain-B0 control by +0.954 percentage points (73.88% vs. 72.92%) across an 88-epoch stateless replay schedule, with learned attention amplitude rising monotonically with semantic depth (27.2% at P3 -> 45.4% at P4 -> 66.3% at P5). Second, we evaluate recurrent weight sharing across repeated MBConv blocks with pass-specific BatchNorm statistics (+1,536 parameters per pass). While post-hoc kernel averaging degrades accuracy to 17.03% and single-template stage tying (-27.6% parameters) plateaus at 66.10%, alternating two shared block templates ([B1, A, B, A]) in Stage 6 cuts total model parameters by 10.9% (582K weights) and recovers by +10.82 points in a single epoch to 70.92% (-1.84 points vs. unshared control).
bullets: BiFPN alone does not beat a plain MBConv trunk, but adding stage attention raises accuracy to 73.15%.
Zero-gated residual attention adapters at P3–P5 achieve 74.02% standalone and a +0.954-point gain over a matched plain-B0 control.
Attention strength increases with semantic depth, from P3 through P5.
Naive kernel averaging and single-template tying substantially hurt accuracy.
Alternating two shared block templates reduces parameters by 10.9% and reaches 70.92% after one epoch, 1.84 points below the unshared control.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Architectural efficiency through targeted global context and alternating weight sharing. (A) Each residual adapter ys = xs + αs · Projs(MHSAs(LN(xs))) initializes at αs = 0 so early convolutional feature learning is undisturbed. By epoch 80, learned branch update-to-input RMS rises monotonically with semantic depth (27.2% at P3 windowed MHSA → 45.4% at P4 global MHSA → 66.3% at P5 global MHSA). Under bit-for-bit identical stateless data replay across 88 epochs, Sparse Attention outperforms Plain-B0 by +0.954 percentage points (73.88% vs. 72.92%; standalone recovery reaches 74.02%). (B) In Stage 6 (the largest parameter stage in EfficientNet-B0), post-hoc kernel averaging degrades zero-shot accuracy to 17.03% and tying all repeated blocks in Stages 4–6 to a single template ([B1, A,A,A]) plateaus at 66.10% (−6.66 pp vs. control), whereas alternating two shared templates ([B1, A,B,A]) with pass-specific BatchNorm statistics reduces total model parameters by 10.9% (582K weights) and recovers to 70.92% in a single continuation epoch.

Figure 2: Full-validation accuracy and resource trajectories across B0–B2 baselines, BiFPN hybrids, and Sparse Stage Attention. While BiFPN-only variants plateau below the plain B0 baseline (69.99%–71.81%), Sparse Stage Attention (P3/P4/P5) achieves the strongest B0-scale trajectory (74.02% standalone; 73.88% vs. 72.92% in the matched pair).

Figure 3: Bit-for-bit matched 88-epoch comparison of Sparse Stage Attention (P3/P4/P5) vs. Plain-B0. Both arms consume identical stateless training streams. Sparse Attention maintains a consistent ∼ 1.0-point lead throughout convergence, finishing at 73.88% vs. 72.92% (+0.954 pp).

papers.title: Where Global Context and Weight Sharing Work in Compact Vision Backbones
papers.tldr: Lightweight stage-specific self-attention improves compact EfficientNet recognition, while carefully designed weight sharing reduces parameters with a moderate accuracy trade-off.

papers.abstract: Generative recommendation (GR) inference differs substantially from conventional LLM serving, featuring long input sequences, wide beam search, and only a few fixed output tokens. Existing LLM serving engines such as vLLM process beams as batched independent sequences, causing redundant KV cache accesses over the shared prompt prefix. Furthermore, vLLM executes each beam search generation step as a separate engine invocation, incurring host-side beam processing overhead between decoding steps and substantial runtime KV block management in PagedAttention. Using Tree Attention, we concatenate beams along the sequence dimension to eliminate redundant KV accesses, and further optimize execution through pre-generated partial-attention masks, static KV cache allocation, loop-unrolled generation dispatch, TorchAir graph compilation, automatic operator fusion, and vocabulary-constrained decoding. Without the use of custom kernels, our approach reduces end-to-end latency by up to 25x over vLLM on Ascend NPUs, and achieves generation latency comparable to a SOTA solution using custom kernels, showing that the generation pipeline should be optimized holistically before resorting to custom kernel development.
authors: Shing Wai Pun, Kai Wu, Pengfei Xia, Hui Zang, Wei Guo, Yong Liu
bullets: Targets GR inference with long prompts, wide beam search, and short fixed outputs.
Uses Tree Attention to share prompt-prefix computation and avoid redundant KV-cache accesses across beams.
Reduces overhead with pre-generated masks, static KV allocation, loop-unrolled dispatch, graph compilation, operator fusion, and constrained decoding.
Achieves latency comparable to a state-of-the-art custom-kernel solution.
Shows that end-to-end pipeline optimization can precede custom-kernel development.

papers.abstract: Kernelized attention methods, which aim to replace the $O(N^2)$ complexity of softmax attention with $O(N)$ alternatives, have been the focus of intense research in the last five years. Despite growing interest, systematic evaluations and fair comparisons across approaches and scales are still missing. We analyze kernelized attention in two halves and highlight prominent limitations on each. On efficiency, FlashAttention achieves lower memory consumption and faster wall-clock time than SOTA kernelized methods during training and in vision transformers across most sequence lengths (with inference-time memory in causal language models the only clear exception), contradicting the core assumption for pure kernelized attention used as a drop-in replacement for softmax. We also discover that reported efficiency gains often fail to reproduce against modern baselines. On quality, current kernelized methods leave gaps of 2-10 points relative to softmax under a unified distillation protocol, and model scala alone does not close these gaps. We show this gap is not intrinsic to kernelization: LARA++, a principled extension of LARA that approximates softmax via importance sampling with adaptive proposal distributions, recovers up to 99% of softmax accuracy. We establish that the gap is closable; however, the computational overhead remains substantial, leaving the efficiency wall intact. Code is available at https://github.com/firatoncel/KernelRealityCheckNeurIPS2026
authors: F{\i}rat \"Oncel, Cem Subakan, Mirco Ravanelli, \c{C}a\u{g}atay Y{\i}ld{\i}z
bullets: Existing efficiency claims for kernelized attention often fail to reproduce against modern baselines.
FlashAttention generally uses less memory and runs faster during training and in vision transformers; causal-language-model inference is the main exception.
Under a unified distillation protocol, current kernelized methods lag softmax by 2–10 points, and scaling alone does not eliminate the gap.
LARA++, using importance sampling with adaptive proposal distributions, recovers up to 99% of softmax accuracy.
The remaining computational overhead means improved quality does not resolve kernelized attention’s efficiency disadvantage.

papers.abstract: When applied to two-dimensional features such as images, Mamba-based methods either flatten the feature map into 1D sequences and fuse multiple scans, which breaks spatial adjacency and multiplies computation, or recurse directly on the 2D grid but rescale the recurrence with a fixed input-independent factor and aggregate only the predecessors on a single anti-diagonal, leaving the discrete step unconstrained by 2D stability theory. We propose \textbf{FM-Mamba}, a native 2D selective state space model built on the general Fornasini--Marchesini (FM) model. Its coupled recurrence evolves along both spatial axes; cross-axis coupling induces a discrete diagonal-predecessor term $\tilde A_0$, and two independent input-dependent step sizes $\Delta_1(i,j)$, $\Delta_2(i,j)$ govern propagation along the two axes, so that the coefficients adapt per position and per direction. A normalized ratio $r_k=a_{0,k}/(a_{1,k}a_{2,k})$ yields a closed-form piecewise bound on the two step sizes; when a configuration falls outside the stable interval the steps are projected onto this bound, and the criterion is re-verified per position after training, which suppresses systematic local amplification without global damping. The recurrence is executed by a dual-diagonal wavefront scan: each update gathers information from two anti-diagonals, and the input enters the current state through a single projection, so that neither training nor inference flattens the feature map. Code is available at https://github.com/BitSsm/FM-Mamba-Runtime
authors: Shengyuan Hu, Yiyong Sun, Weihang Shan, Yongzhe Chang
bullets: Addresses inefficiency and spatial-adjacency loss from flattening 2D features, as well as stability limitations in prior recursive 2D Mamba methods.
Uses the Fornasini–Marchesini model with coupled recurrences along both spatial axes and a diagonal-predecessor interaction.
Employs two input-dependent step sizes per position and direction, constrained by a closed-form stability bound and projected when unstable.
Implements a dual-diagonal wavefront scan without flattening during training or inference.
Scope: the abstract describes the architecture and stability mechanism but does not report experimental results.

papers.abstract: Sparse attention models read a few blocks of keys for every query at a fixed budget and can lose much of their long-context retrieval accuracy at that budget. We ask where this loss is made. Using exact attention mass selection at the shipped budget as an oracle, we show that the selector under-ranks the needle rather than running out of budget. We find attention heads that miss the needle by running a calibration probe that teacher-forces the answer and reads two quantities in every head. The first is the needle attention that the selector forfeits, and the second is the share of the answer's log-probability that fixing the head's selection restores, integrated along the path from the shipped selector to full attention. Four checkpoints of the InfLLM-V2 family and NOSA-8B lose multi-key retrieval in the same three blind heads, which attend to the needle while a mean-pooled key summary dilutes its single decisive token. Full attention in those heads or a 4-bit scorer that keeps the shipped budget recovers most of the loss without training. On MiniCPM4.1-8B at 64K, either fix lifts multi-key retrieval accuracy from 54.1 to 97.5%, level with full attention in every head. In production serving engines, full attention in those heads keeps 84 to 89% of the time to first token (TTFT) that sparse attention saves at 32K to 128K context length. Beyond the InfLLM-V2 selector lineage, one unified rule flags attention heads above a threshold swept on each checkpoint until they close most of the gap to full attention on calibration prompts. A similar small set of blind attention heads carry the loss for the SeerAttention-R gates, NSA, and DashAttention, whereas many such heads exist in MoBA. On Qwen3-8B with the SeerAttention-R gates, full attention in 18 of 288 key-value heads lifts multi-key retrieval accuracy from 29.8 to 97.7%.
bullets: Exact-attention analysis shows the main issue is selector mis-ranking of relevant blocks, not exhausting the fixed budget.
A teacher-forced calibration probe identifies heads that attend to the needle but lose it when mean-pooled key summaries dilute its decisive token.
For InfLLM-V2 and NOSA-8B, the same three blind heads explain much of the multi-key retrieval loss; similar patterns appear in several other sparse-attention methods.
Repairing flagged heads with full attention or a 4-bit scorer preserves the shipped budget and recovers most of the loss without training.
Reported gains include MiniCPM4.1-8B improving from 54.1% to 97.5% at 64K, while selective full attention retains 84–89% of sparse attention’s TTFT savings; MoBA shows many more blind heads.

figures.caption: Figure 4: Method overview. (a) InfLLM-V2 scores each block from mean-pooled keys, gathers the top-k blocks and attends to them in every head. (b) A needle probe, run once per checkpoint, compares the shipped selection with exact attention mass at the same budget, which explains the failure, and keeps the heads with the largest gain of fixing their selection. (c) In the flagged heads, full attention reads every block, and every other head keeps the shipped selector. A 4-bit scorer that keeps the shipped budget can replace full attention in those heads.

Per key-value head, the needle recall that the shipped selector loses against exact mass, times the attention the head puts on the needle block, on calibration prompts at 32K, or 16K for Dash-8B and NSA-8B. The blind head attends to the needle, but the pooled score leaves the needle block below the shipped cutoff, while exact mass keeps it.

papers.selection_reason: Diagnoses and repairs block selection in sparse attention for long-context LLMs; directly relevant to efficient attention and long-context models.
papers.title: Lost in a Few Heads: Diagnosing and Repairing Block Selection in Sparse Attention
papers.tldr: A small number of blind attention heads cause most sparse-attention retrieval failures, and selectively repairing them largely restores full-attention accuracy at much of sparse serving’s speed benefit.

papers.abstract: Rapid advances in image and video generation have enabled high-fidelity synthesis at higher resolutions and longer durations, making the quadratic cost of dense self-attention a major bottleneck as visual token sequences grow. Sparse attention seeks to preserve generation quality at lower computational cost by retaining informative query-key interactions and omitting less consequential ones, with end-to-end gains depending on the cost of constructing sparse support and the efficiency with which the system maps the resulting workload to hardware. We survey sparse attention for visual generation through a 4+1+3 analytical framework that links algorithmic design to system implementation. The framework examines how static and dynamic methods use source information and the evidence derived from it to decide which interactions to retain and at what granularity, while accounting for the roles of reuse in reducing repeated computation and correction in compensating for omitted contributions. We relate these algorithmic choices to their implementation on hardware through the framework's three system dimensions of data organization, execution, and dataflow. We summarize common evaluation metrics and discuss open challenges and research directions, providing researchers and practitioners with a reference for the joint design of sparse attention algorithms and systems.
authors: Majun Zhang, Yuan Guo, Decheng Wu, Jiayang Xu, Changhao Pan, Fan Zhuo, Xiaoda Yang, Chenyuhao Wen, Zhou Zhao
bullets: Dense self-attention becomes a major bottleneck as image and video token sequences grow.
The proposed 4+1+3 framework analyzes static and dynamic sparsity, selection granularity, reuse, and correction for omitted interactions.
It links algorithmic choices to three system dimensions: data organization, execution, and dataflow.
The survey reviews evaluation metrics, implementation considerations, open challenges, and future research directions.

figures.caption: Fig. 3. The 4+1+3 framework for sparse attention. The source, evidence construction, granularity, and support specification determine which query–key pairs are retained. Reuse avoids repeating work across denoising steps, and correction compensates for contributions from omitted pairs. Data organization, execution, and dataflow determine how the sparse attention workload runs on hardware. The tile example shows how the shape of the support affects computation. papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) have achieved strong performance in generation based video editing, but suffer from high inference latency due to the long token sequences formed by conditioning inputs and generated videos. Although training-free sparse attention reduces this cost, existing methods typically apply a fixed retention ratio or a single threshold shared across all tokens. In this work, we view video editing as conditional generation and identify a key insight: attention demand varies significantly both across different key sources (e.g., source videos, reference images, audio, text, and generated videos) and across queries within each source. Motivated by this, we propose QASK-Edit (Query-Adaptive Sparsity over Key Sources for Video Editing), a training-free sparse attention framework that allocates computation independently for each query and key source. Specifically, for each query, QASK-Edit considers both the attention mass and approximation risk of each block. It then evaluates candidate routing thresholds against each key source's risk budget, choosing exact computation or approximations to dynamically adjust sparsity for each query. Extensive experiments on three video editing models demonstrate that QASK-Edit achieves up to $1.46\times$ end-to-end speedup over dense attention pipeline while preserving both editing quality and unedited region fidelity. Furthermore, QASK-Edit generalizes directly to Reference-to-Video generation, delivering up to $1.36\times$ speedup while maintaining generation quality.

This routing threshold then determines whether to perform exact or approximate calculations. papers.abstract: Generating consistent multi-view RGB images and normal maps from a single input image provides complementary appearance and geometric cues for 3D reconstruction. However, maintaining cross-view consistency requires information exchange across viewpoints, and dense cross-view attention becomes computationally expensive as the number of views and spatial resolution increase. In this paper, we propose Global-Local Proxy Attention (GLPA) to reduce cross-view communication costs while preserving fine-grained within-view processing. Specifically, GLPA retains full-resolution interactions within each view and uses compact global proxies for cross-view communication. To further leverage the exchanged information, GLPA incorporates iterative proxy refinement, which rebuilds the proxies from updated features and reuses the same attention parameters for subsequent interactions within a single denoising step. We evaluate GLPA on two structurally different diffusion backbones, FLUX and Stable Diffusion. Experiments on FLUX show that GLPA achieves a $2.65\times$ speedup in attention computation per denoising step over dense attention, while improving reconstruction IoU from 0.6849 to 0.7019 and reducing NVS LPIPS from 0.086 to 0.076. Results on Stable Diffusion further demonstrate the effectiveness of GLPA, with a $1.80\times$ attention speedup and improvements across all five quality metrics.

On FLUX, it provides a 2.65× attention-computation speedup, higher reconstruction IoU, and lower NVS LPIPS; Stable Diffusion shows a 1.80× speedup and improvements on all five reported metrics.

papers.abstract: Video diffusion transformers rely on 3D full attention over tens of thousands of spatiotemporal tokens, and its quadratic cost dominates inference latency. Sparse attention reduces this cost, but existing methods face a dilemma: static methods apply predefined masks and cannot capture input-dependent attention, whereas dynamic methods reconstruct the sparse mask repeatedly, paying online to rediscover positional structure that is largely stable across inputs. To this end, we propose PoCoAttn, a training-free sparse attention framework that separates input-stable from input-dependent attention and resolves the former offline and the latter online. PoCoAttn features: (1) A relative-offset analysis of 3D query-key pairs, which shows that video attention decomposes into an input-stable positional prior that carries most of the attention mass and a small content-dependent residual. (2) A position-content collaborative sparse attention mechanism, which retrieves positional keys from offline-calibrated tables, selects content keys online with a head-adaptive ratio between the two sources, and compensates for the discarded keys to approximate full attention. (3) A step-adaptive budget allocation algorithm, which models how early-step sparse attention errors are amplified along the denoising trajectory and derives the optimal sparsity budget per step. Extensive experiments across four video diffusion models and three tasks show that PoCoAttn consistently achieves a better speed-fidelity Pareto frontier than state-of-the-art (SOTA) methods, improving PSNR by 1.9 to 5.0 dB over baselines and delivering up to 4.1$\times$ attention and 2.0$\times$ denoising speedups over dense FlashAttention-3 attention.
authors: Jianwen Wu, Meiling Wang, Junkang Zhou, Yipeng Shen, Haoran You
bullets: Addresses the quadratic cost of 3D full attention over large spatiotemporal token sequences.
Separates mostly input-stable positional attention from a smaller input-dependent content residual.
Retrieves positional keys from offline-calibrated tables, selects content keys online, and compensates for discarded keys.
Allocates sparsity budgets across denoising steps based on error amplification, with head-adaptive position/content ratios.
Across four video diffusion models and three tasks, reports 1.9–5.0 dB PSNR gains over baselines and up to 4.1× attention and 2.0× denoising speedups versus dense FlashAttention-3.

papers.abstract: We present a Scalable Windowed Axial-attention Neural Receiver (SWAN-Rx) for multiple-input multiple-output orthogonal frequency-division multiplexing (MIMO-OFDM) systems. The receiver improves reception accuracy and reduces forward-pass computation while supporting frozen-weight reuse across bandwidth allocations and channel conditions. It combines a common resource-element representation of received observations and pilot context with alternating time-axis and local frequency-axis attention. Shared parameters and relative positional information permit soft detection across allocation lengths without inference-time parameter updates. At fixed subcarrier spacing, model configuration, and symbol count, bounded frequency neighborhoods give linear growth of forward-pass computation with bandwidth. Evaluations compatible with the 5G New Radio physical layer reuse weights trained on four physical resource blocks (PRBs) at up to 273 PRBs and on unseen channels. At the training bandwidth, SWAN-Rx achieves lower pre- and post-decoding bit error rates than the implemented three-step neural receiver (NRX) and DeepRx-MIMO baselines, with 16.9% and 39.7% fewer parameters and 56.3% and 35.7% fewer forward-pass operations, respectively. The same weights achieve lower pre-decoding error rates than these baselines throughout the evaluated bandwidth-extrapolation and 16-PRB channel-transfer tests, with an estimated 0.4-0.9 dB signal-to-noise ratio reduction relative to NRX at a pre-decoding error rate of $10^{-2}$ in the 16-PRB tests.

In 5G NR-compatible evaluations, it outperformed the implemented NRX and DeepRx-MIMO baselines at training bandwidth and retained lower pre-decoding error across bandwidth extrapolation and 16-PRB channel-transfer tests.

papers.abstract: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) enable on-device image generation and editing but incur high attention costs at high resolutions. Existing sparse attention reduces computation, yet dynamic sparsity introduces preprocessing and irregular data accesses that poorly fit mobile NPUs. We present DiT.XPU, a sparse DiT inference framework for heterogeneous mobile SoCs. DiT.XPU combines tile-aligned sparse attention with anchor-based error compensation by exploiting slowly varying dense-sparse output residuals across denoising steps. Heterogeneous XPU collaboration overlaps NPU dense attention with GPU sparse calibration, while mask-guided dataflow reduces data transfers and layout conversion by overlapping data movement with computation. Across five DiT models on two Snapdragon smartphones, DiT.XPU achieves up to 1.56x end-to-end denoising speedup over the Hexagon-NPU backend and 11.5x attention-kernel speedup over the fastest alternative, while preserving generation quality close to dense attention. Code is available at https://github.com/IF-LAB-PKU/dit.xpu.

papers.abstract: Sequence models represent past context at different resolutions, using token-level keys and values, fixed-size recurrent states, or hierarchies of compressed summaries. Full attention supports strong associative recall but requires quadratic work during training and prefill and a linearly growing key-value cache during inference. Linear attention and state-space models reduce these costs through fixed-size recurrent memory, but this compression can limit recall. Log-linear attention offers a middle ground by maintaining logarithmically many state matrices. However, its hierarchy favors finer resolution near the current query while compressing earlier context into coarser summaries. To complement this allocation of resolution, we introduce bilateral log-linear attention, which pairs the existing hierarchy with a second hierarchy anchored at the sequence origin. By combining their reads, the two branches provide finer access to both early and recent context while remaining causal. We derive recurrent and chunkwise parallel formulations for the added branch, preserving log-linear training and prefill work, logarithmic decoding work per token, and logarithmic persistent state storage at fixed feature dimensions and chunk size. In multi-query associative recall, this design raises mean overall test accuracy from 76.37% to 96.12% over forward log-linear attention across multiple training seeds. For pretrained language models under approximate parameter matching, it raises the mean score on six selected RULER needle-in-a-haystack tasks from 26.97% to 50.03% at a context length of 6144 tokens. In the same setting, bilateral attention also outperforms forward log-linear attention on seven of eight downstream retrieval tasks, including question answering and information extraction.
bullets: Full attention recalls well but has quadratic training/prefill cost and a linearly growing inference cache.
The method complements the existing recent-context hierarchy with a second hierarchy anchored at the sequence start, enabling finer access to both early and recent tokens while remaining causal.
Recurrent and chunkwise-parallel formulations retain log-linear training and prefill work, logarithmic decoding per token, and logarithmic persistent state storage.
Mean associative-recall accuracy improves from 76.37% to 96.12%; selected RULER retrieval scores improve from 26.97% to 50.03% at 6,144-token context.
It outperforms forward log-linear attention on seven of eight downstream retrieval tasks, including question answering and information extraction.

papers.title: Bilateral Log-Linear Attention
papers.tldr: Bilateral log-linear attention improves long-context recall by adding a second, origin-anchored hierarchy while preserving logarithmic computational and memory costs.

papers.abstract: A vision transformer read at a higher resolution than it was trained at spreads each attention row over many more patches, yet every row must still hand out exactly one unit of weight. A law of softmax attention predicts that a growing crowd of bounded scores dilutes the attention on any patch or register whose score stays fixed. The same law gives a remedy that needs no training: multiply every score, the sink's included, by the ratio of the logarithms of the test and training token counts. Given sufficient margins at the training resolution, this keeps the attention on a match when one is present, and on a sink such as a register when none is, though trained models need not meet those margins. We test these predictions in public vision transformers and in controlled models read far above their training token count. Attention spreads as predicted. Registers lose their share, though production models compensate in part, and the rescaling holds the share of DINOv2's registers nearly level. Applied at test time without training, the rescaling recovers part of the lost accuracy in nearly every model, with absolute or rotary positions and with registers, and on images with native detail. The calibrated multiplier rises with the logarithmic ratio on average and varies across models. Its rise is steeper than the square-root rule used in image generators; in controlled models the log ratio is also more accurate, while in the public models the two rules' accuracy difference remains unresolved. The rescaling does not restore the attention a model learned, and why it helps, beyond countering the dilution, remains open.
bullets: Problem: Increasing resolution creates more tokens while each attention row still sums to one, reducing attention to fixed-score patches or register tokens.
Method: Apply a training-free multiplier to all attention scores, including sink/register scores, based on the logarithmic ratio of test and training token counts.
Finding: Attention dilution and register-share loss appear as predicted; the rescaling keeps DINOv2 register attention nearly stable.
Result: Test-time rescaling recovers part of the lost accuracy across nearly every tested model, including models with absolute or rotary positional encodings and native-detail images.
Scope: The method does not fully restore learned attention, and the mechanism beyond counteracting dilution remains unresolved; its advantage over square-root scaling varies by model.

papers.selection_reason: Analyzes attention dilution in Vision Transformers at high resolution and proposes a training-free rescaling method to recover accuracy.
papers.title: Spread Too Thin: How Higher Resolution Dilutes a Vision Transformer's Attention, and a Training-Free Rescaling
papers.tldr: Higher-resolution inputs dilute vision-transformer attention across more patches, but scaling attention scores by the log ratio of test-to-training token counts can recover some lost accuracy without retraining.

papers.abstract: Linear-attention language models replace a growing key-value cache with a recurrent state of fixed size. On an edge FPGA, this state can exceed the on-chip memory and must be paged to external memory. This paper asks whether such paging dominates the cost of decoding (generating tokens). We built a hardware tile that computes one complete layer of a custom 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model on an Agilex 5 FPGA and pages its recurrent state. The model state needs 6.2 MiB, whereas the device has 0.87 MiB of block memory. Paging adds 26.0 MB of memory traffic per decoded token, at most 11.2 percent of the calculated total. On the board at 75 MHz, with synthetic weights, one token takes 11.15 ms in this layer. The matrix-vector products with the weights take about 62 percent of this time and the state phase, including the paging, 13 percent. The tile is one node of a multicast mesh of tri-mode processing elements. We measure the error of the fixed-point arithmetic against floating point and check that the hardware agrees bit for bit with a fixed-point reference. In simulation, the state logic agrees with the reference on all 18 recurrent layers. On the board, six builds pass all 30 runs of 64 tokens and two runs of 1,024 tokens. For this model and memory interface, the delivery of the weights limits the decoding performance, and the recurrent state does not. State paging is therefore practical for such a model on an edge FPGA.
bullets: The 6.2 MiB recurrent state exceeds the FPGA’s 0.87 MiB on-chip memory, requiring external-memory paging.
Paging adds 26.0 MB of traffic per token, but accounts for at most 11.2% of calculated total cost; the state phase takes 13% of measured layer time.
The tile computes a complete layer of a 369-million-parameter hybrid Gated DeltaNet model at 75 MHz, with one token taking 11.15 ms using synthetic weights.
Fixed-point hardware matches a fixed-point reference bit for bit; state logic also agrees across all 18 recurrent layers in simulation and all reported board tests.
The conclusion is scoped to this model and memory interface: weight delivery remains the decoding bottleneck.

papers.selection_reason: Hardware-efficient linear-attention LLM inference with paged recurrent state; directly fits efficient attention and memory-efficiency topics.
papers.title: The State Is Not the Bottleneck: A Paged-State Gated-DeltaNet Tile on a Tri-Mode Multicast Mesh, Bit-Exact from RTL to Silicon
papers.tldr: For this edge-FPGA Gated DeltaNet tile, paging the recurrent state is practical because weight delivery—not state paging—limits token-decoding performance.

papers.abstract: Feed-forward multi-view transformers such as VGGT recover the cameras and geometry of a video in one pass, but the cost of their cross-frame attention grows quadratically with the frame count, and their accuracy drops on long videos. Most remedies approximate attention over all frames within a budget or select a few keys by their content. We hypothesize that the keys of a long video can be chosen without looking at its content, and our experiments on VGGT and $\pi^3$ support it: a few dozen evenly spread frames can serve as the keys of every frame. We present EcoVGGT, a training-free inference framework whose keys form a Pinned Key Set of 31 such frames. A pin pass stores their tokens in a Scene Cache, and the other frames read it in independent batches that reproduce joint inference with these keys exactly, at a constant cost per frame. An Online Stream updates the pinned frames during recording. Six middle global blocks align the frames and form a reusable VGGT module: the Alignment Score reads their attention to flag failures, and Alignment Refocusing reduces them by fine-tuning only these blocks (3.6 GPU hours). EcoVGGT ($\pi^3$) matches the success rate of $\pi^3$ on 1,000-frame ScanNet videos at 13.8 times its speed. With refocusing, EcoVGGT (VGGT) raises the success rate of VGGT from 70% to 82% at 8.5 times its speed on 500 frames. EcoVGGT reconstructs 4,000 frames on one GPU, and EcoVGGT ($\pi^3$) streams 1,000 frames at 18.6 frames per second with the lowest online absolute trajectory error.
authors: Hongsen Cao, Shanxin Yuan, Mona Jaber, Ahmed Sayed
bullets: Addresses quadratic cross-frame attention costs and accuracy degradation on long videos.
Uses a training-free Pinned Key Set of 31 frames, cached once and reused by independently processed frames.
Supports online streaming by updating pinned frames during recording.
An Alignment Score detects failures, while Alignment Refocusing fine-tunes six global blocks to improve robustness.
On long ScanNet videos, it matches or improves baseline success rates while achieving substantially higher speed and scaling to thousands of frames on one GPU.

papers.selection_reason: Proposes a training-free efficient inference method for feed-forward 3D reconstruction from long videos, relevant to token pruning and efficient attention.
papers.title: EcoVGGT: Pinned-Key Inference for Efficient and Streamable Feed-Forward 3D Reconstruction from Long Videos
papers.tldr: EcoVGGT makes long-video feed-forward 3D reconstruction efficient and streamable by using a small, fixed set of evenly spaced key frames.

papers.abstract: Attention is essential for modeling spatio-temporal dependencies in video diffusion transformers, but its quadratic cost makes it a major inference bottleneck. Its high sparsity offers an opportunity to accelerate generation by focusing computation on important interactions. However, accuracy and execution favor different granularities: each query attends to its own key tokens, whereas GPU kernels work on tiles. We present Token2Tile, a training-free sparse attention operator that combines per-query scoring and a per-query residual with tile execution. An online low-rank space, computed directly from queries and keys to preserve attention logits, makes clustering, scoring, and residual approximation efficient. Token2Tile unites query-specific selections to allocate exact work across query clusters, then packs the selected keys into GPU tiles. On MiniMax-H3 and Wan2.1-14B, Token2Tile delivers 1.48-1.54x end-to-end speedup over dense FlashAttention-3 with VBench scores within 0.5 points of dense. At comparable speeds on H3, it improves PSNR over SOL and SubBlock by 5.5-6.8 dB; on Wan, it exceeds SOL by 4.6-4.8 dB while running faster.
authors: Xuecheng Wu, Aichen Feng, Jinyan Chen, Qingjie Zhao, Julien Lai
bullets: Targets the quadratic inference cost of spatio-temporal attention in video diffusion transformers.
Uses per-query scoring and residual approximation in an online low-rank space derived from queries and keys.
Clusters query-specific selections and packs selected keys into GPU tiles for efficient execution.
Achieves 1.48–1.54× end-to-end speedup over dense FlashAttention-3, with VBench within 0.5 points of dense.
Outperforms SOL and SubBlock in PSNR at comparable or higher speeds on the evaluated models.

papers.selection_reason: Training-free sparse attention for video diffusion transformers, improves efficiency.
papers.title: Token2Tile: Token-Wise Sparse Attention with Tile Execution through a Low-Rank Space for Video DiTs
papers.tldr: Token2Tile accelerates video diffusion attention by combining token-level sparsity with GPU-friendly tile execution while preserving near-dense quality.

papers.abstract: Multi-view 3D transformers such as VGGT reconstruct a scene from a set of unposed images in a single forward pass, predicting camera poses, depth and 3D points, but the cost of their global attention grows quadratically with the num- ber of images. Accelerators borrowed from large language models assume that each token attends to only a few oth- ers; on these models they lose accuracy or gain little speed. We study the global attention of three multi-view transform- ers on seven datasets and find that every layer plays one of three roles: it averages over the whole scene, matches points across many images, or anchors on the first image, whose coordinates the outputs use. Building on this anal- ysis, we propose Regime-AWare ATTention Approximation (RAWATTA), a training-free method that runs attention in 8- bit precision and keeps 16-bit precision only in the layers where a worst-case calibration check requires it. Its fast set- ting, RAWATTA-Fast, also approximates attention in a few averaging and anchoring layers, while matching layers and the first image keep all their keys. On a 12 GB GPU at 50 im- ages, RAWATTA runs VGGT faster than the released code, mostly through our CUDA engine, and loses at most about one point of pose accuracy (AUC@3) on any dataset; RAWATTA-Fast is slightly faster and less accurate. Both fit 200 images, where the released code runs out of memory at 100.
authors: Muhammed Izzet Sezer, Sevval Belkis Dikkaya
bullets: Global attention in multi-view 3D transformers is costly because its complexity grows quadratically with the number of images.
The study identifies three layer roles: scene-wide averaging, cross-image point matching, and anchoring to the first image.
RAWATTA uses 8-bit attention by default and retains 16-bit precision when a worst-case calibration check requires it.
RAWATTA-Fast additionally approximates attention in selected averaging and anchoring layers while preserving full keys for matching layers and the first image.
On VGGT, RAWATTA is faster than the released implementation, loses at most about one AUC@3 pose-accuracy point, and supports 200 images on a 12 GB GPU where the baseline runs out of memory at 100.

papers.abstract: Adversarial training is one of the most reliable defenses against adversarial attacks, but its high computational cost must generally be paid anew for each task. Robust foundation models offer a promising alternative: adversarially pretrain a model once and then transfer its robustness to downstream tasks through lightweight adaptation. However, a fundamental question remains open: can robustness acquired during pretraining transfer to unseen tasks without further adversarial training? In this study, we answer this question affirmatively. A single model adversarially pretrained at scale can achieve optimal robustness on new tasks without additional task-specific training. Specifically, we show that, for a family of Gaussian-mixture classification tasks, a sufficiently deep linear transformer adversarially trained across tasks can asymptotically attain the robust Bayes error on previously unseen tasks through in-context learning from clean demonstrations. By contrast, a standardly trained model cannot. We further analyze convergence under gradient flow, an accuracy--robustness trade-off, and demonstration complexity.
bullets: Studies whether robustness learned during pretraining transfers to new tasks.
Shows this transfer for Gaussian-mixture classification with sufficiently deep linear transformers.
Adversarially trained models asymptotically achieve robust Bayes error on unseen tasks via clean demonstrations.
Standardly trained models do not achieve the same robust performance.
Also analyzes gradient-flow convergence, the accuracy–robustness trade-off, and demonstration complexity.

papers.title: Adversarially Trained Linear Transformers Are Optimal Robust In-Context Learners for Gaussian Mixtures
papers.tldr: Adversarially pretrained deep linear transformers can transfer optimal robustness to unseen Gaussian-mixture classification tasks through clean in-context demonstrations, without task-specific adversarial training.

papers.abstract: Accurate bioactivity prediction is a central challenge in early-stage drug discovery, as individual assays often contain too few measurements to train reliable models independently. Meta-learning offers a principled approach to this few-shot setting, but assay heterogeneity may limit its effectiveness. Here, we test this hypothesis and show that meta-learning performance degrades as meta-training tasks become more heterogeneous. To address this, we introduce MetaHeta, a meta-learning framework that accounts for assay heterogeneity by conditioning predictions on auxiliary data from related assays, with relatedness defined flexibly from available assay information. The architecture of MetaHeta combines linear attention over large auxiliary datasets with exact attention over scarce task-specific context, enabling efficient scaling to the former without compromising exact attention over the latter. We demonstrate the benefits of our approach on assays from ChEMBL and BindingDB, improving few-shot bioactivity prediction and downstream compound prioritization in retrospective Bayesian optimization.
bullets: Few-shot assay datasets often lack enough measurements for reliable independent models.
Meta-learning performance declines when meta-training assays are highly heterogeneous.
MetaHeta conditions predictions on auxiliary data from flexibly defined related assays.
It combines linear attention for large auxiliary datasets with exact attention for scarce task-specific context.
Experiments on ChEMBL and BindingDB show improved prediction and retrospective Bayesian-optimization compound prioritization.

When Daux = ∅, the auxiliary branch is skipped. Finally, an output MLP parameterizes a mean-field Gaussian predictive distribution. papers.abstract: We present UniSpark-9B, a unified multimodal model that investigates hybrid attention for visual understanding and generation. Built on a Mixture-of-Transformer-Experts backbone with approximately 9B parameters in each branch, UniSpark combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation. Autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching jointly support visual question answering, text-to-image generation, instruction-guided editing, and interleaved text-image prediction. In interleaved generation, noisy visual targets are isolated from subsequent predictions, while clean visual representations provide context for later outputs. A blockwise protocol enforces this distinction through attention masks in full-attention layers and recurrent-state retention rules in linear-attention layers. The selected training sources contain 159.7M generation samples, 213.4M understanding samples, and 624.8K interleaved sequences. A four-stage curriculum jointly trains multimodal understanding and visual generation, refining answer accuracy and instruction following while extending image synthesis to 2K. UniSpark scores 2470.3 on MME-S and 0.83 on GenEval. Qualitative examples further illustrate its capabilities in interleaved image generation, video synthesis, and video editing. Together, these results demonstrate that hybrid attention provides an effective backbone for unified multimodal understanding and generation.
authors: Jiancheng Pan, Yuzheng Liu, Hengyuan Cao, Qiyuan Zhang, Yangyan Li, Biao Gong, Zheng Zhang, Ka Long Cheng, Xinyang Wang, Yujun Shen
bullets: Combines full attention for explicit token interactions with GatedDeltaNet linear attention for compact context propagation.
Uses autoregressive text prediction and visual flow matching across visual question answering, text-to-image generation, editing, and interleaved generation.
Applies blockwise attention masks and recurrent-state rules to separate noisy visual targets from later predictions.
Trained with a four-stage curriculum spanning multimodal understanding, generation, and interleaved sequences, with image synthesis extended to 2K.
Reports 2470.3 on MME-S and 0.83 on GenEval; qualitative examples include video synthesis and editing.

papers.abstract: Expert-parallel Mixture-of-Experts decoding is latency bound: each layer serializes a token exchange, a grouped GEMM over routed experts, and a combine, while only a few tokens per rank are in flight. Prior GC-MoE fused these phases into one persistent, Green-Context-partitioned CUDA Graph on Hopper (SM90) and datacenter Blackwell (SM100). This paper rebuilds the operator for SM120 (compute capability 12.0, e.g. RTX PRO 5000) over PCIe. SM120 exposes block-scaled tensor cores only through warp-level mma.sync.aligned.kind::mxf8f6f4: no tensor memory, no two-CTA MMA, no cluster multicast. We rebuild the kernel around a swap-AB warp-level block-scaled MMA with FP4 weights in the register A operand and FP8 activations in B, plus SM120-specific mechanisms: scale-byte selection through MMA immediates, a compact-weights path, an adaptive token-tile geometry, an expert-granular streaming dispatch with a batched bulk-pull engine and a 64-bit deduplicating pull cache, full-width BF16 returns drained by resident relay copiers over a position-major arena, and shared experts folded into the compute role. On 8xRTX PRO 5000 over PCIe the operator is 1.522x and 1.387x faster than the FlashInfer CuTe DSL W4A8 MegaMoE and the Cake MegaMoE across 18 decode points (18/18 wins each), and 1.388x faster than Cake with shared experts fused; all 94 numerical cases and 752 per-rank checks pass, at cross-operator cosine similarity of at least 0.9999997.
authors: Yong Li, Haoyu Wang, Kan Liu, Tao Lan
bullets: Targets latency from serialized token exchange, expert GEMM, and combine phases in low-concurrency decoding.
Uses warp-level FP8×FP4 block-scaled MMA with register-resident FP4 weights and SM120-specific scale selection.
Overlaps expert-granular dispatch, computation, and returns using adaptive tiling, batched pulls, a deduplicating cache, and resident relay copiers.
On 8× RTX PRO 5000 GPUs, it wins all 18 tested decode points against two baselines and also outperforms shared-expert-fused Cake.
All reported numerical cases and per-rank checks pass, with cross-operator cosine similarity of at least 0.9999997.
